newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil chief of staff to look into Patricia coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil chief of staff to look into Patricia coffee.

text.p: Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has said he will ask his chief of staff to examine a request to resolve debt problems linked to "Operation Patricia", a coffee exporter official said.
Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation, sent the request in a letter to Cardoso in the middle of this month.
"I received a reply from the president a few days ago in which he said he was sending the document to his chief of staff recommending that it be examined," Aranha said.
"This means that I am expecting to hear more," he added.
"Operation Patricia" involved 18 companies which, acting for the now-defunct Brazilian Coffee Institute (IBC), bought a total of 635,000 60-kg bags of coffee on the London exchange in 1986.
The idea was to maximise Brazil's revenue from its coffee exports which were sharply down that year because of a drought.
Trade houses were to buy futures contracts, take delivery of of coffee and then in theory were to be paid back either in coffee or in cash.
However since 1987, the companies have only received $15 million, around one tenth of what they are owed.
In April 1990, four companies won a judgement against the IBC in the U.K High Court which ordered the IBC to compensate the four firms.
The same year the IBC was liquidated, with the Brazilian government assuming all outstanding obligations.
Most recently a sequestration order was served on the Milan branch of Germany's Deutsche Bank ordering the seizure of Brazilian government assets following the issue of a 500 billion lire bond.
All monies from the bond have arrived in Brazil however without interference, Central Bank officials have said.
